nb_upper_dawn_wall.blurb: A trad wall in the Dawn Walls section of the Cochrane Lane Cliffs near Welsford, perched above the Lower Dawn Wall. All 19 climbs are traditional lines, running from an easy 5.4 route up through a solid block of 5.9 and 5.10 cracks and corners, with a handful of 5.11 and 5.12 testpieces at the top end. Mid-grade climbers have several popular choices here. Routes begin from a roomy ledge, and the usual way onto it is to climb the first pitch of a neighbouring route, so expect a bit of roped climbing just to reach the start. A good stop for a trad day built around moderate to hard crack climbing.

nb_amphitheatre.blurb: A big bowl-shaped section of the Cochrane Lane Cliffs at Welsford, set above Cheekbone Corner. It holds 16 climbs, nearly all trad, with the bulk of them between 5.9 and 5.12 and a couple of hard 5.13 lines plus a few easier options at the bottom of the range. Several of the best-known routes sit in the 5.7 to 5.11 band, including a two-pitch 5.10 line. The walk in goes past a cave and then scrambles up a boulder field into the bowl, so it feels a little tucked away. Best suited to climbers comfortable placing their own gear on sustained mid-grade and harder cracks.

nb_exfoliated.blurb: A crag within the Cochrane Lane Cliffs near Welsford that mixes 10 trad lines with 6 bolted ones. The grades lean hard: a few easier routes around 5.6 to 5.8, a thin middle, then a cluster of 5.12s and one 5.13 at the top. Large trees at the foot of the cliff keep the climbs damp for a while after rain, so pick a dry spell. Most routes finish at tree anchors on top, which makes setting up a top rope simple. The trail in leaves the farm field at its back right corner and is rarely used.

nb_waterfall_wall.blurb: A face-climbing wall near the middle of the Cochrane Lane Cliffs at Welsford, named for the seasonal waterfall beside it. The rock is just off vertical, and the 16 climbs are 11 trad and 5 sport, with a strong concentration at 5.10 and a few 5.11s and 5.12s plus one easy line. A trickle keeps the base of the left-hand routes wet through summer, while the three sport lines at the right end dry fast and catch plenty of sun, which makes them workable on mild winter days. The frozen fall also draws ice climbers. The way up is through a boulder field into the middle of the wall.

nb_simpson_wall.blurb: A friendly trad wall in the Cochrane Lane Cliffs at Welsford, with 16 climbs that run from about 5.3 up to 5.11 and clump heavily in the 5.5 to 5.8 range. That makes it one of the better spots in the cliffs for newer trad leaders, and the classics have names borrowed from a well-known cartoon family. Routes are long, around 35 m, so bring a 70 m rope to get down. The face collects a lot of sun. The approach is short and easy along the main path, past the lookout and then left at a fork.

nb_monster_wall_main_wall.blurb: The upper tier of the Hampton Marsh crag near the Kennebecasis shore, reached by a short scramble through the trees above the roadside wall. Monster Wall is short, steep and bouldery, a rare dose of overhanging rock for New Brunswick, while Main Wall is taller with gently overhanging faces and roofs on its left and dirtier vertical rock to the right. Of 16 climbs, 15 are sport, mostly 5.11 to 5.13 with a couple of 5.14s, so this is hard-climber territory. The rock is rhyolite and can break, so a helmet is wise. Fixed lines help with the steep ground below.
